label: Distinguish explicit cost, implicit cost, accounting profit, economic profit, and normal profit.
finding: Hard often supplies accounting profit rather than asking students to classify receipts and expenses. EL-002 incorrectly offsets higher accounting profit against lower opportunity cost. Retain multi-owner comparisons and normal-profit fundamentals.

label: Analyze short-run production using total, marginal, and average product.
finding: Hard derives MP from genuine output schedules; total-product shape and marginal/average distinctions are already represented.

label: Calculate and interpret fixed, variable, total, average, and marginal costs.
finding: Hard includes reconstructed AFC/AVC/ATC, missing-output inference, and cost schedules. Retain broad coverage.

label: Explain relationships among production measures and short-run cost curves.
finding: Most Hard curve relationships are strong. H-044 asks an intersection tautology despite feedback teaching the average maximum; strengthen the inference.

label: Analyze how fixed costs, input prices, and productivity changes affect cost curves.
finding: Fixed/sunk and wage/productivity effects are covered. Selected upper-tier items can better compare the current commitment with a later capacity decision.

label: Evaluate long-run average cost, economies of scale, diseconomies of scale, and minimum efficient scale.
finding: Hard scale/MES schedules are strong. Some Elite/Legendary items remain label or one-step lookup; strengthen plant-choice integration without confusing short-run diminishing returns with scale.

label: Explain the assumptions and price-taking behavior of perfectly competitive firms.
finding: Price taking, entry conditions, differentiation limits and information assumptions are covered.

label: Calculate and interpret total, average, and marginal revenue for a competitive firm.
finding: Revenue calculations and market-price transmission to horizontal AR/MR are covered.

label: Determine the profit-maximizing or loss-minimizing output using marginal analysis.
finding: Discrete marginal output choice and rising-MC conditions are already strong at Hard.

label: Calculate and interpret profit, loss, break-even, and shutdown outcomes.
finding: Loss-but-produce and shutdown coverage is strong; selected graph questions isolate revenue/cost rather than combining output, profit, and operation.

label: Derive and interpret the competitive firm’s short-run supply behavior.
finding: Supply aggregation and fixed-versus-variable changes exist; add explicit market supply/cost-shock transmission to a representative firm, with magnitudes rather than an unsupported universal profit direction.

label: Analyze entry, exit, long-run equilibrium, industry cost conditions, and efficiency.
finding: Entry/exit direction and industry-cost conditions exist. Several upper-tier items ask only one stage; reconstruct full market supply, price, firm MR/output and zero-profit sequence.

label: Explain monopoly, market power, and the major barriers to entry.
finding: Legal, resource, scale and network barriers are adequately applied.

label: Calculate and interpret demand, total revenue, average revenue, and marginal revenue for a monopolist.
finding: Demand/MR/TR and price-effect reasoning are covered.

label: Determine the monopolist’s profit-maximizing output and price using marginal analysis.
finding: Hard includes rule recitation with unused numerical data; strengthen actual Q to demand-price to profit reasoning using approved graphs.

label: Calculate and interpret monopoly profit, loss, shutdown, and cost changes.
finding: Legendary-boss profit/loss records omit price and output and depend on another randomly drawn question. Repair every affected record.

label: Compare monopoly and competitive outcomes using surplus, efficiency, and deadweight loss.
finding: Hard compares monopoly/efficient output and foregone mutually beneficial trades; retain transfer-versus-DWL and innovation tradeoffs.

label: Evaluate natural-monopoly regulation, price discrimination, and monopoly-policy tradeoffs.
finding: Regulation and first/third-degree discrimination are selected. H-040 says regulated while feedback uses unregulated monopoly. Upper-tier regulatory comparisons are fragmented across separate records.

label: Explain the characteristics of monopolistic competition and the sources of product differentiation.
finding: Close substitutes and differentiation distinguish the model from monopoly and price taking.

label: Determine short-run output, price, profit, loss, and shutdown outcomes using marginal analysis.
finding: Six Hard, ten Legendary and twelve Legendary-boss profit questions omit indispensable Q/P inputs. Some choices repeat the same wrong rule semantically; correct standalone completeness and rounding.

label: Analyze how entry and exit change an existing firm’s demand and economic profit.
finding: Entry/exit demand changes and stopping conditions are already present, including reversal after fixed-cost shocks.

label: Explain long-run zero-profit equilibrium, tangency, markup, and excess capacity.
finding: Approved graphs cover profit, tangency, markup and excess capacity. Retain good Hard multi-step examples; strengthen selected upper-tier inference.

label: Analyze advertising, branding, quality, and other forms of nonprice competition.
finding: Advertising, quality, signaling, costs, demand shifts and elasticity differences are covered.

label: Evaluate product variety, efficiency, welfare tradeoffs, and real-world market classifications.
finding: Existing welfare tradeoff is sound. Use graph-based policy evaluation to integrate markup, excess capacity and valued variety.

label: Explain oligopoly, strategic interdependence, entry barriers, and market concentration.
finding: Four Hard HHI questions square an aggregated Other bar without saying whether it is one firm. Establish the missing assumption; retain concentration limitations.

label: Read payoff matrices and identify best responses, dominant strategies, and Nash equilibria.
finding: Hard already uses matrices, including multiple/no pure equilibria. Six Legendary best-response questions do not specify the opponent action. Strengthen upper-tier comparison of all equilibria with joint totals, retaining social-welfare limits.

label: Analyze prisoner’s-dilemma incentives, collusion, cartel behavior, and cheating.
finding: Collusion instability, deviation and transfer-versus-loss distinctions are strong.

label: Evaluate repeated interaction, punishment, credibility, tacit coordination, and price wars.
finding: Repeated-game present values and punishment/monitoring are already beyond ordinary exam demand.

label: Analyze entry deterrence, nonprice competition, price leadership, and supplemental oligopoly models.
finding: Credible threats, entry deterrence, price leadership and predation evidence are selected. Tying and resale-price maintenance are not.

label: Evaluate cartel welfare, mergers, concentration, innovation, and antitrust tradeoffs.
finding: Concentration versus market power is well covered. Add a concrete agreement example within existing antitrust rationale, without adding statute-specific doctrine.
